questions.question: A dairy owner sells 528 litres of milk daily in one litre packets of 3 varieties – full cream, toned and double toned. Sales of toned milk packets are 80% higher than those of full cream milk packets, and sales of double toned milk packets are 60% lower than those of toned milk packets. How many packets of double toned milk does he sell per day?
questions.solution:
Given:

A dairy owner sells 528 litres of milk daily in one litre packets of 3 varieties – full cream, toned and double toned. 

Sales of toned milk packets are 80% higher than those of full cream milk packets.

Sales of double toned milk packets are 60% lower than those of toned milk packets.

Calculation:

Let Q packet of full cream milk be sold.

Number of packets of toned milk sold = Q + Q × 80%

⇒ 1.8Q

Number of packets of double toned milk sold = 1.8Q - 1.8 × 60%

⇒ 0.72Q

According to the question,

Q + 1.8Q + 0.72Q = 528

⇒ 3.52Q = 528

⇒ Q = 528/3.52

⇒ Q = 150

Now, number of doble toned milk sold per day = 150 × 0.72

⇒ 108

∴ He sells 108 packets of double toned milk per day.

questions.question: Find the ratio of the LCM of the first four prime numbers to the HCF of the first three prime numbers.
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

First, four prime numbers are 2, 3, 5 and 7

There can't be any common number that can divide all the numbers completely.

So, the LCM is the product.

LCM = 2 × 3 × 5 × 7

⇒ 210

Similarly for HCF

HCF of 2, 3, 5 is 1

So, ratio = 210 : 1

**∴ The required answer is 210 : 1.**

questions.question: The perimeter of a circular plot is 440 m. Around it is a circular path 5 m wide. The area of ​​the path (in m², assuming π =(22)/(7)) will be approximately?
questions.solution:
Given:

The perimeter of a circular plot is 440 m. Around it is a circular path 5 m wide.

Concept used:

Perimeter of a circle = 2πR

Area of a circle = πR²

R = Radius of the circle

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9c15d5c7e9247879e7caa1eb4a98be0ade2af18bf1aaadfc4da62c803a7f587e.png] 

Radius of the circular plot = 440 ÷ 2π

⇒ 70 m

Area of the plot = (π × 70²) m²

Area of the circular plot including the path = π × (70 + 5)²

⇒ (π × 752) m2

Now, the area of the circular path = (π × 752) - (π × 702)

⇒ π(75² - 70²)

⇒ π(75 + 70)(75 - 70)

⇒ 22/7 × 145 × 5

⇒ 2278.571 ≈ 2278.6 m²

**∴ The area of the path is 2278.6 m2.**

questions.question: B takes five times the number of days taken by A to complete a piece of work. Working together, they complete the work in 15 days. In how many days will A alone complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

B takes five times the number of days taken by A to complete a piece of work. Working together, they complete the work in 15 days.

Concept used:

Total work = Work done per day × Total time taken

Efficiencies (work done per day) of workers is inversely proportional to the time taken by workers to complete a particular task.

Calculation:

Let A and B do 5p and p units work a day respectively.

Total work = 15(5p + p) = 90p units

Now, A alone will complete the work = 90p ÷ 5p

⇒ 18 days

∴ A alone will complete the work in 18 days.

questions.question: By selling an article for Rs 2,900, a shopkeeper makes a profit of 16%. If he had sold it for Rs 3,050, what would have been his percentage profit?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

By selling an article for Rs 2,900, a shopkeeper makes a profit of 16%.

New selling price = Rs. 3050

**Concept used:**

Selling price = Cost price × profit%

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

Cost price × 116% = 2900

⇒ Cost price = 2900 × (100/116)

⇒ 2500

New profit = 3050 - 2500

⇒ 550

Profit % = (550/2500) × 100

⇒ 22

**∴ His percentage of profit would be 22%.**

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 24 days. B and C together can complete it in 30 days. If the efficiency of A is twice that of C, then in how many days will B alone complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

A and B together can do a piece of work in 24 days. B and C together can complete it in 30 days

The efficiency of A is twice that of C.

Concept used:

Total work = Work done per day × Total time taken

Calculation:

LCM (24, 30) = 120 units

Let efficiencies of A, B, and C be represented by A, B, and C respectively.

So, A = 2C

According to the question,

A + B = 120/24

⇒ A + B = 5

⇒ 2C + B = 5 ....(1)

B + C = 120/30

⇒ B + C = 4 ....(2)

(1) - (2),

2C + B - B - C = 5 - 4

⇒ C = 1

Putting C = 1 in (2),

B = 3

Now, B will alone complete the work in = 120/3

⇒ 40 days

∴ B alone will complete the work in 40 days.

questions.question: A, B and C are three numbers. A is 45% more than B and C is 60% less than A. By what percent (to the nearest integer) B is more than C?
questions.solution:

A, B and C are three numbers. A is 45% more than B and C is 60% less than A.

Let B be 100.

A = 100 + 100 × 45% = 145

C = 145 - 145 × 60% = 58

Now, % more = {{100 - 58} over 58} times 100\%

⇒ 72.41%

∴ B is 72% more than C.

questions.question: The compound interest of a sum of Rs. 75,000 at a fixed annual rate of interest compounded on an annual basis in 2 years is Rs. 6,120. If the interest is compounded quarterly, what will be the sum of Rs. 1,00,000 received after one year at the same rate of interest (in Rs., up to two places of decimal)?​
questions.solution:
Given:

The compound interest of a sum of Rs. 75,000 at a fixed annual rate of interest compounded on an annual basis in 2 years is Rs. 6,120.

Concept used:

In case of the compound interest,

Amount = P(1 + R/100)N

CI = P(1 + R/100)N - P

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

N = Time in years

Calculation:

Let the interest rate be R%.

According to the question,

75000(1 + R/100)² - 75000 = 6120

⇒ (1 + R/100)2 = (75000 + 6120)/75000

⇒ (1 + R/100)2 = 1.0816

⇒ (1 + R/100)2 = 1.04²

​⇒ 1 + R/100 = 1.04

⇒ R/100 = 1.04 - 1

⇒ R = 4

When the interest is compounded quarterly,

The amount becomes = 100000(1 + {{4over 4} over 100})⁴ × ¹

⇒ 100000(1.01)⁴

⇒ Rs. 104060.40

**∴ The amount becomes Rs. 104060.40.**

questions.question: A certain sum of money, in 4 years at the same rate of simple interest per annum, amounts to Rs. 12,420 and in 7 years Rs. 14,985. How much is that amount?
questions.solution:
Given:

A certain sum of money, in 4 years at the same rate of simple interest per annum, amounts to Rs. 12,420 and in 7 years Rs. 14,985.

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P + SI

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

Interest in 3 years = 14985 - 12420 = Rs. 2565

Interest per year = 2565/3 = Rs. 855

Let the principal amount and the rate of interest be Rs. P and R% respectively.

According to the question,

(P × 1 × R)/100 = 855

⇒ PR = 85500

According to the question,

P + (P × 4 × R)/100 = 12420 ....(1)

P + (P × 7 × R)/100 = 14985 ....(2)

(2) + (1),

2P + 12PR/100 = 27405

⇒ 2P + (11 × 85500)/100 = 27405

⇒ 2P = 27405 - (11 × 855)

⇒ 2P = 18000

⇒ P = 9000

∴ The principal amount is Rs. 9000.

questions.question: If bananas are sold at a price of Rs. 10 per banana instead of Rs. 7 per banana, then the difference between the selling prices of some bananas is Rs. 990. If the cost price of all the bananas is Rs. 1,980, and if the profit earned is 18%, then what will be the selling price (in Rs.) of the ten bananas?
questions.solution:
Given:

If bananas are sold at a price of Rs. 10 per banana instead of Rs. 7 per banana, then the difference between the selling prices of some bananas is Rs. 990.

The cost price of all the bananas is Rs. 1,980.

Profit earned = 18%

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Gain%

Calculation:

Let the cost price of N bananas be Rs. Q each.

According to the question,

10N - 7N = 990

⇒ 3N = 990

⇒ N = 330 ....(1)

According to the question,

NQ = 1980

⇒ 330 × Q = 1980 (From 1)

⇒ Q = 6

Let the selling price of each banana be Rs. P.

According to the question,

330P = 1980 + 1980 × 18%

⇒ P = (1980 × 1.18)/330

⇒ P = 7.08

Now, the selling price of 10 bananas = 10 × 7.08

⇒ Rs. 70.80

∴ The selling price of 10 bananas is Rs. 70.80.

questions.question: If 51, x, 72 and 96 are proportional, then what will be the mean ratio between (2x + 8) and (x + 13)?
questions.solution:
Given:

51, x, 72 and 96 are proportional

Concept used:

If A : B :: C : D then (B × C) = (A × D)

Calculation:

According to the concept,

x × 72 = 51 × 96

⇒ x = 4896/72

⇒ x = 68

(2x + 8) = (2 × 68 + 8)

⇒ 144

(x + 13) = (68 + 13)

⇒ 81

Mean ratio = √(144 × 81)

⇒ 108

∴ The mean proportion is 108.

questions.question: Two trains A and B of equal length are running on parallel tracks in the same direction with speeds of 64.8 km/h and 50.4 km/h respectively. Train A crosses train B in one minute. Find the length (in m) of each train.
questions.solution:
Given:

When a train completely crosses another train, it basically crosses the sum of the lengths of the two trains.

Concept used:

Relative speed is the difference between individual speeds while two objects run in the same direction.

Distance = Speed × Time

When a train completely crosses another train, it basically crosses the sum of the lengths of the two trains.

Calculation:

Relative speed = 64.8 - 50.4 = 14.4 km/h

14.4 km/h = 14.4 ÷ 18/5 = 4 m/s

So, the sum of the length of train A and B = 4 × 60

⇒ 240 m

Now, the length of each train = 240/2 = 120 m

∴ The length of each train is 120 m.

questions.question: The average weight of 23 students was recorded as 53 kg. On including the weight of a teacher, the average weight increased by 100 g. Find the weight (in kg) of the teacher.
questions.solution:
Given:

The average weight of 23 students was recorded as 53 kg. On including the weight of a teacher, the average weight increased by 100 g.

Concept used:

Total = Average × Number of entities

Calculation:

Total weight of 23 students = 23 × 53

⇒ 1219 kg

100 g = 0.1 kg

New average including the teacher = 53 + 0.1 = 53.1 kg

Now, the weight of the teacher = 53.1 × (23 + 1) - 53 × 23

⇒ 55.4 kg

∴ The weight of the teacher is 55.4 kg.

questions.question: Shopkeeper A, gives two successive discounts of 8% and 12% on the marked price of Rs.500. Another shopkeeper B allows a single discount of 20% on an article of the same marked price. Find the difference in their selling prices.
questions.solution:
Given:

Shopkeeper A, gives two successive discounts of 8% and 12% on the marked price of Rs. Rs 500.

Another shopkeeper B allows a single discount of 20% on an article of the same marked price.

Concept used:

Final discount percentage after two successive discounts of A% and B% = (A + B - {AB over 100})\%

Calculation:

Final discount given by Shopkeeper A = 8 + 12 - (12 × 8)/100 = 19.04%

Now, the the difference in their selling prices = 500 × (20 - 19.04)%

⇒ 500 × 0.96%

⇒ Rs. 4.80

∴ The difference in their selling prices is Rs. 4.80.

questions.question: An amount of Rs. 7,800 is divided into A, B and C such that B's share belongs to (1)/(3) of A's share and C's share is 20% more than B's share. Find the share of A.
questions.solution:
Given:

An amount of Rs. 7,800 is divided into A, B and C such that B's share belongs to (1)/(3) of A's share and C's share is 20% more than B's share.

Calculation:

Let B's share be P.

C's share = P + P × 20% = 1.2P

A's share = P ÷ 1/3 = 3P

According to the question,

3P + 1.2P + P = 7800

⇒ 5.2P = 7800

⇒ P = 7800/5.2

⇒ P = 1500

Now, A's share = 1500 × 3 = Rs. 4500

∴ A's share is Rs. 4500.
